Supplementary Information

Appendix S1 Device Impairment Models

This section provides the full mathematical models for the six impairment sources that degrade the ideal inner-product computation of eq. 6.

Weight quantization.

MRR transmission is programmed via electro-optic tuning with finite precision. We model the quantized weight as

w^n,j=round​(wn,j⋅2b)2b,\hat{w}_{n,j}=\frac{\text{round}(w_{n,j}\cdot 2^{b})}{2^{b}}, (S1)

where bb is the effective bit precision. Values of b=4b=4–88 are considered, corresponding to 16–256 distinguishable transmission levels.

Thermal drift.

After initial calibration, the MRR resonance wavelength drifts due to ambient temperature fluctuations. We model the drift as a Gaussian random walk:

Δ​λ0​(t)=∑i=1t/Δ​t𝒩⁡(0,σdrift2),\Delta\lambda_{0}(t)=\sum_{i=1}^{t/\Delta t}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\text{drift}}^{2}), (S2)

with σdrift\sigma_{\text{drift}} chosen to produce a standard deviation of 0.01 nm to 0.1 nm0.01\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}0.1\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} over a calibration interval TcalT_{\text{cal}}. The resulting weight error is

Δ​w=|∂T∂λ|​Δ​λ0≈8​Q2​Dmaxλ02⋅Δ​λ0,\Delta w=\left|\frac{\partial T}{\partial\lambda}\right|\Delta\lambda_{0}\approx\frac{8Q^{2}D_{\max}}{\lambda_{0}^{2}}\cdot\Delta\lambda_{0}, (S3)

evaluated at the operating point on the MRR Lorentzian. Note that the i.i.d. Gaussian model above does not capture spatially correlated drift (e.g., center-to-edge temperature gradients across the chip), which could cause systematic bias in the inner-product scores rather than zero-mean random noise; such gradients would require a correlated noise model or per-region calibration.

Insertion loss.

Each MRR introduces an off-resonance insertion loss ILMRR≈0.02 dB to 0.05 dB\text{IL}_{\text{MRR}}\approx$0.02\text{\,}\mathrm{dB}0.05\text{\,}\mathrm{dB}$, and the 1×N1\times N splitter contributes ILsplit\text{IL}_{\text{split}} from eq. 8. The total channel loss is

ILtotal=ILsplit+d⋅ILMRR+ILwg,\text{IL}_{\text{total}}=\text{IL}_{\text{split}}+d\cdot\text{IL}_{\text{MRR}}+\text{IL}_{\text{wg}}, (S4)

where ILwg\text{IL}_{\text{wg}} accounts for waveguide propagation loss (∼\sim0.3 dB0.3\text{\,}\mathrm{dB} for TFLN). High insertion loss reduces the SNR at the photodetector and increases the required laser power.

Photodetector noise.

The photocurrent at each detector includes shot noise and thermal noise:

σI2=2​e​Iph​Δ​f+4​kB​TRL​Δ​f+NEP2⋅Δ​f,\sigma_{I}^{2}=2eI_{\text{ph}}\,\Delta f+\frac{4k_{B}T}{R_{L}}\,\Delta f+\text{NEP}^{2}\cdot\Delta f, (S5)

where IphI_{\text{ph}} is the signal photocurrent, Δ​f\Delta f is the detection bandwidth, RLR_{L} is the load resistance, and NEP is the noise-equivalent power of the photodetector (∼10 pW\sim$10\text{\,}\mathrm{pW}$ for Ge-on-Si) [1, 2]. The noise introduces a random perturbation to the inner-product score, potentially reordering the top-kk ranking.

MRR crosstalk.

Adjacent MRRs on the same bus waveguide can exhibit spectral overlap if the channel spacing is insufficient relative to the MRR linewidth. We model inter-channel crosstalk as an additive interference with isolation of −15 dB to −30 dB-15\text{\,}\mathrm{dB}-30\text{\,}\mathrm{dB}:

yn=∑j=1dwn,j​sj+∑j=1d∑m≠jχj,m​wn,m​sm,y_{n}=\sum_{j=1}^{d}w_{n,j}\,s_{j}+\sum_{j=1}^{d}\sum_{m\neq j}\chi_{j,m}\,w_{n,m}\,s_{m}, (S6)

where χj,m\chi_{j,m} is the crosstalk coefficient from channel mm to channel jj [3].

Input DAC noise.

The finite resolution and integral nonlinearity (INL) of the input DACs contribute an additional noise floor on the query sketch values. At bDAC=6b_{\text{DAC}}=6 bits, the quantization noise standard deviation is σDAC=2−bDAC/12≈0.0045\sigma_{\text{DAC}}=2^{-b_{\text{DAC}}}/\sqrt{12}\approx 0.0045.

The Prism latency is the sum of the five pipeline stages:

tPRISM=tDAC+topt+tPD+tADC+ttop-​k,t_{\text{PRISM}}=t_{\text{DAC}}+t_{\text{opt}}+t_{\text{PD}}+t_{\text{ADC}}+t_{\text{top-}k}, (S7)

where the optical propagation time toptt_{\text{opt}} includes the modulator response, waveguide transit, and MRR ring-down time.

Appendix S4 Retrieval Head Detailed Results

Appendix S5 Crossover Derivation

This section provides the full algebraic derivation of the energy crossover point n∗n^{*} summarized in Sec. VI.5.

The total decode cost per token for a retrieval head consists of two terms:

Ctotal=Cselect​(n)+Cfetch​(n,k),C_{\text{total}}=C_{\text{select}}(n)+C_{\text{fetch}}(n,k), (S8)

where CselectC_{\text{select}} is the cost of determining which blocks to fetch and CfetchC_{\text{fetch}} is the cost of reading and computing attention over the selected blocks.

For the GPU full scan baseline, no selection is needed (k=N=n/Bk=N=n/B), so the energy cost of reading all nn keys is

CGPU=CfetchGPU​(n,n/B)=2​dh​n​bprec⋅Ebyte,C_{\text{GPU}}=C_{\text{fetch}}^{\text{GPU}}(n,n/B)=2\,d_{h}\,n\,b_{\text{prec}}\cdot E_{\text{byte}}, (S9)

where Ebyte≈31 pJ/BE_{\text{byte}}\approx$31\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{B}$ is the energy per byte for HBM3 memory access (H100 GPU) [5].

For Prism, the cost is

CPRISM=CselectPRISM​(n)+CfetchGPU​(n,k⋅B),C_{\text{PRISM}}=C_{\text{select}}^{\text{PRISM}}(n)+C_{\text{fetch}}^{\text{GPU}}(n,k\cdot B), (S10)

where CselectPRISMC_{\text{select}}^{\text{PRISM}} is the dynamic energy of the photonic evaluation (laser, DAC, modulator, PD, ADC):

CselectPRISM≈Edynamic,C_{\text{select}}^{\text{PRISM}}\approx E_{\text{dynamic}}, (S11)

Note that on the TFLN platform, the static MRR tuning power is near zero (capacitive EO), so the selection cost is dominated entirely by the dynamic components (∼2290 pJ{\sim}$2290\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{J}$ per query, table 3). The fetch cost is reduced by the selection ratio k/Nk/N:

CfetchGPU​(n,k⋅B)=2​dh​k​B​bprec⋅Ebyte.C_{\text{fetch}}^{\text{GPU}}(n,k\cdot B)=2\,d_{h}\,k\,B\,b_{\text{prec}}\cdot E_{\text{byte}}. (S12)

The crossover occurs when CPRISM<CGPUC_{\text{PRISM}}<C_{\text{GPU}}, i.e., when the memory access energy saved by not fetching (N−k)(N-k) blocks exceeds the energy cost of operating the photonic selector.

Setting CPRISM=CGPUC_{\text{PRISM}}=C_{\text{GPU}} and solving for nn yields:

n∗=CselectPRISM2​dh​bprec​Ebyte​(1−k​B/n∗),n^{*}=\frac{C_{\text{select}}^{\text{PRISM}}}{2\,d_{h}\,b_{\text{prec}}\,E_{\text{byte}}\,(1-k\,B/n^{*})}, (S13)

which must be solved self-consistently since kk and N=n/BN=n/B both depend on nn. In practice, kk is a fixed parameter (e.g., k=32k=32), so the selection ratio k​B/n→0k\,B/n\to 0 as n→∞n\to\infty, and the crossover simplifies to

n∗≈CselectPRISM2​dh​bprec​Ebyte.n^{*}\approx\frac{C_{\text{select}}^{\text{PRISM}}}{2\,d_{h}\,b_{\text{prec}}\,E_{\text{byte}}}. (S14)

Appendix S6 WDM Channel Limits

The maximum number of WDM channels dd is constrained by the MRR free spectral range (FSR), the available optical bandwidth, and inter-channel crosstalk.

Single-FSR constraint.

For a TFLN MRR with radius R=20 µ​mR=$20\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro m}$, the FSR is approximately 8.3 nm8.3\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} (at λ0=1550 nm\lambda_{0}=$1550\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}$, as in table 1). At a channel spacing of Δ​λch=1.6 nm\Delta\lambda_{\text{ch}}=$1.6\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}$ (200 GHz200\text{\,}\mathrm{GHz} on the ITU grid) [6], the maximum number of non-aliased channels within one FSR is

dmax(1-FSR)=⌊FSRΔ​λch⌋=⌊8.31.6⌋=5.d_{\max}^{\text{(1-FSR)}}=\left\lfloor\frac{\text{FSR}}{\Delta\lambda_{\text{ch}}}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac{8.3}{1.6}\right\rfloor=5. (S15)

This is clearly insufficient for the d=32d=32–128128 range targeted by Prism.

FSR extension techniques.

Vernier-coupled dual-ring filters or cascaded MRRs with slightly different radii can extend the effective FSR to ∼\sim50 nm50\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} or more [7, 8], limited by the least common multiple of the individual FSRs. With an extended FSR of 50 nm50\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} and Δ​λch=1.6 nm\Delta\lambda_{\text{ch}}=$1.6\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}$:

dmax(Vernier)=⌊501.6⌋≈30.d_{\max}^{\text{(Vernier)}}=\left\lfloor\frac{50}{1.6}\right\rfloor\approx 30. (S16)

Band-limited operation.

The usable optical bandwidth depends on the operating band:

  • •

    C-band (1530–1565 nm1565\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}): 35 nm35\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} →\rightarrow practical limit d∼20d\sim 20–3030 without FSR extension;

  • •

    C+L band (1530–1625 nm1625\text{\,}\mathrm{nm}): 95 nm95\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} →\rightarrow d∼60d\sim 60.

For d>60d>60, extending to the S-band or using 0.8 nm0.8\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} (100 GHz100\text{\,}\mathrm{GHz}) channel spacing is necessary, at the cost of tighter crosstalk margins. In practice, achieving d=128d=128 requires both FSR extension and C+L+S band operation, representing a more aggressive photonic design point.

S6.1 Balanced Photodetection for Signed Weights

The add-drop MRR configuration provides both through-port transmission Tthrough​(Δ​λ)T_{\text{through}}(\Delta\lambda) and complementary drop-port transmission Tdrop​(Δ​λ)=1−Tthrough​(Δ​λ)T_{\text{drop}}(\Delta\lambda)=1-T_{\text{through}}(\Delta\lambda) (for a lossless ring). A balanced photodetector pair measures the differential signal:

w=Tthrough−Tdrop=2​Tthrough−1∈[−1,+1].w=T_{\text{through}}-T_{\text{drop}}=2\,T_{\text{through}}-1\in[-1,\,+1]. (S17)

This mapping naturally encodes signed weights without doubling the MRR count (as required by split encoding) or discarding sign information (as in ReLU projection). The noise model for balanced detection yields shot noise variance σ2=2​e​ℛ​P0​Δ​f\sigma^{2}=2e\mathcal{R}P_{0}\Delta f, independent of the programmed weight, since power is conserved: Pthrough+Pdrop=P0P_{\text{through}}+P_{\text{drop}}=P_{0} [1].

Appendix S7 Multi-Head Serving with GQA

A natural concern is whether serving all retrieval heads requires replicating the weight bank for each head. In Qwen2.5-7B, 102 out of 112 KV heads are retrieval heads at 8K context (table S3). However, GQA [9] reduces the number of independent KV heads to HKV=4H_{\text{KV}}=4—each KV head is shared across H/HKV=7H/H_{\text{KV}}=7 query heads. The weight bank stores block signatures derived from key vectors, so it operates at the KV-head granularity, not the query-head granularity. This means only 4 independent weight bank configurations are needed per layer, not 102.

Two strategies can serve these 4 KV heads:

  1. 1.

    Time-multiplexed reuse. A single weight bank is reprogrammed sequentially for each of the 4 KV heads. On the TFLN platform, EO tuning settles in ∼1 ns{\sim}$1\text{\,}\mathrm{ns}$ (RC-limited), so reprogramming 4 heads adds only ∼4 ns{\sim}$4\text{\,}\mathrm{ns}$—negligible compared to the subsequent KV block fetch (∼5 µ​s{\sim}$5\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro s}$).

  2. 2.

    Parallel replication. Four weight banks are deployed in parallel, one per KV head. This requires 4×d×N=4×64×1024=262 1444\times d\times N=4\times 64\times 1024=$262\,144$ MRRs total—a 4×4\times increase over the single-head case but within the scalability limits discussed in Sec. VII.1.

GQA thus reduces the multi-head serving problem from 102 independent banks (one per retrieval head) to just 4, making both time-multiplexed and spatially-parallel approaches practical. For Qwen3-8B (HKV=8H_{\text{KV}}=8), the same argument applies with 8 KV heads, still far below the 258 retrieval heads.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
